Persistent memory makes LLM assistants persistent collaborators, but it also creates an unmanaged input channel into future responses. We study benign memory contamination: degradation caused by ordinary memory-system behavior, without an attacker, jailbreak, or attacker-poisoned record. The seeded-recursion probe uses a controlled contaminated write-back to exercise recursion; it does not model an attacker. We contribute a taxonomy of six mechanisms: semantic drift, provenance collapse, scope bleed, temporal staleness, recursive compounding, and summarization loss. We also introduce CONTAM-Bench, an open, spec-driven benchmark evaluated here as a nine-scenario pilot with a personalization-retention control, and a proposed mitigation architecture based on scoped namespaces, provenance tags, raw fidelity, and decay by fact class. We report an ablation over seven configurations using one subject model and TF-IDF retrieval, followed by five repetitions of each scenario-configuration cell. On the targeted probes, the namespacing arm excluded cross-domain distractors from retrieval and the TTL arm excluded the stale record from retrieval in all five repetitions; response-level outcomes are reported separately in the tables. On the provenance probe, tags and raw fidelity each yielded five machine-resolved clean outcomes; these are clean response-verdict outcomes, not utility measurements. In the seeded-recursion case (CB-VAL-009), logged relevance-gate decisions discarded premise-denying context while retaining a contaminated write-back. We call this observed failure presupposition capture and propose contradiction preservation as a proposed safeguard; its downstream efficacy was not evaluated. Of 350 scored rounds, 52 remain unresolved pending human review. These are within-scenario observations for these nine scenarios, one subject model, and five repetitions per cell; they do not estimate real-world prevalence or model-independent mitigation efficacy. CB-VAL-009 is a controlled seed for recursion, not observed benign behavior; the benign-contamination framing rests on the other scenarios. The proposed taxonomy supplies one falsifiable criterion and one hand-authored scenario per mechanism, rather than six empirically demonstrated mechanisms. Machine-resolved contamination outcomes occurred for provenance collapse and scope bleed; CB-VAL-005 had one second-round contaminated output but no contaminated first round and therefore did not demonstrate natural compounding. Semantic drift and summarization loss had only clean machine outcomes, while temporal staleness was clean or unresolved. In these evaluated cases, scoped namespaces and TTL decay excluded the targeted records from retrieval. Per-scenario outcomes are reported without a general ordering among mitigations.
